name: Caroline Yates
note: Confirmed by unanimous voice vote to the Graduate Advisory Council on 17 September 2024 -- a university-committee appointment, not on its own proof of a Senate seat. But 'Senator Yates' is addressed directly and answers questions in floor debate on 1 October 2024 (Resolution 4-24-F) and 15 October 2024 (Bill 5-24-F), appears in the Senate's own roll-call absence list on 19 November 2024, and is addressed a fourth time by a guest speaker on 11 February 2025. No other Yates appears anywhere in the corpus. Internal comparison strengthens this: Kiersten Washington, a non-senator resolution author in these same minutes, is never once called 'Senator Washington' despite authoring two resolutions -- 'Senator' in this corpus tracks real Senate membership, not a loose courtesy title. By 19 November 2024 the Graduate Advisory Council report reads 'No Graduate Senator,' where 'Caroline Yates' had been listed weeks before, suggesting her seat's own title may have been 'Graduate Senator' and that she had left it by then -- inference, not proof, so the seat is left unset. Strongest evidence found outside these 17 files: an already-published Herald article, already cited in years.json under 2025-26, reports 'Senator Caroline Yates' authoring a Go With the Flow bill on 11 November 2025 -- independent confirmation that she held a Senate seat as a continuing member in a later year, which corroborates that the 2024-25 'Senator Yates' references reflect a genuine seat rather than a loose or mistaken usage. No bill-authorship line naming her seat was found in the 2024-25 corpus itself, so this remains real evidence but weaker than the other 19 entries.

name: Malick Ibrahim
note: Listed by full name as 'Malick Ibrahim, Member' of the Organizational Aid Board from 15 October 2024 (Bill 9-24-F contacts block), alongside several confirmed senators. 'Senator Ibrahim' is used from the very first meeting in the corpus (9/10/24: 'Senator Ibrahim made a motion to adjourn') and in absence lists through 29 October 2024 (9/24, 10/1, 10/15, 10/22, 10/29). He does not appear as a bare surname in any absence list after that -- an independent, already-published Herald article, already cited in years.json's 2024-25 events, reports that the Judicial Council voted 7-0 on 6 November 2024 to remove 'Senators Malick Ibrahim, Myricle Gholston and Karisha Petty' from their seats for excessive unexcused absences. That article names him 'Senator Malick Ibrahim' directly and in full, which is stronger, independent confirmation of Senate membership than anything found in the 17 minutes files, and it also explains why he disappears from later minutes. He was originally elected a freshman senator in the fall 2023 special election for the 23rd Senate (per a separate Herald article already in years.json's 2023-24 events, 'electing Savanna Kurtz, Malick Ibrahim and Chloe Ralston as freshman senators') and evidently continued into the 24th Senate before his November 2024 removal. No bill-authorship line naming a 2024-25 seat title was found, so seat is left unset.

name: Myricle Gholston
note: Removed from her Senate seat by the Judicial Council on 6 November 2024, alongside Malick Ibrahim and Karisha Petty, after accumulating at least six unexcused absences and a second censure.

name: Karisha Petty
note: Removed from her Senate seat by the Judicial Council on 6 November 2024, alongside Malick Ibrahim and Myricle Gholston, after accumulating at least six unexcused absences and a second censure. She later told the Herald her absences were due to medical issues.
